mainTopic: Does a חופה with a woman forbidden to the man have legal force? This covers whether it stops her from eating תרומה, and רב ששת's proof from the סוטה oath.
overview: The גמרא asks whether entering the חופה with a כהן she may not marry stops a woman from eating תרומה, and looks for an argument among תנאים about this. It first ties the question to the argument of רבי מאיר versus רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון about קידושין. It rejects that link, because קידושין and חופה differ in two ways. It then brings a ברייתא where the תנא קמא lets such women eat תרומה after חופה, while רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says they may not. That proof is also pushed off: רבי ישמעאל may simply agree with רבי מאיר and be borrowing the תנא קמא's wording. Next, רב עמרם reports רב ששת's rule that a חופה counts even with women who are forbidden to the man, proven from the סוטה oath that mentions an ארוסה. After rejecting two possible cases, the גמרא settles on one where she was warned and secluded herself as an ארוסה and then entered the חופה without relations. רבא challenges this, and רמי בר חמא answers by adding that her betrothed had been with her earlier in her father's house. The גמרא then starts to test the matching case of a שומרת יבם, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Linking the question to the argument about קידושין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the question about חופה depends on the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון about קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר, who says קידושין disqualifies her, חופה also disqualifies her. According to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, who say קידושין does not disqualify her, חופה also does not disqualify her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that its question about חופה already depends on a known argument between תנאים about קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about a woman who is not allowed to marry a certain כהן. רבי מאיר holds that even קידושין to him stops her from eating תרומה, so the גמרא assumes he would say the same about חופה. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון hold that קידושין does not stop her, so the גמרא assumes the same would be true of חופה.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
The wedding canopy, the second stage of marriage
Disqualify / it disqualifies (here, from eating תרומה)
Also, too

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Meir, who says betrothal disqualifies,
phrases.notes: This is about a woman the כהן is not allowed to marry. The question is whether she loses the right to eat תרומה.

phrases.english: the wedding canopy also disqualifies.
According to Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon,
who say betrothal does not disqualify,
the wedding canopy also does not disqualify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the suggestion begun before this section that the question about חופה is an argument among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of whether חופה disqualifies her from תרומה is an argument among תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The argument between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון about whether קידושין disqualifies her

steps.title: Maybe רבי מאיר is only strict about קידושין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the link: רבי מאיר might be strict only about קידושין, because קידושין actually acquires the woman and חופה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do you know? Perhaps רבי מאיר only said this there about קידושין, which acquires her. But חופה, which does not acquire her, does not disqualify her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says the comparison between קידושין and חופה may not hold for רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין is the act that legally makes her his wife, so it could have the power to disqualify her. Entering the חופה is not an act of acquiring, so רבי מאיר might say it has no such effect. If so, his view tells us nothing about חופה.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you know?
Perhaps
He only said this far (his ruling applies only to this case)
Acquires her (legally makes her his wife)

phrases.english: And from where do you know?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Meir only said it there
about betrothal, which acquires her,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חוּפָּה דְּלָא קָנֵי לַהּ — לָא.
phrases.english: but the wedding canopy, which does not acquire her, does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed link from step 1 as it applies to רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the part of the proof that relies on רבי מאיר's opinion
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: קידושין and חופה are not the same, because only קידושין acquires her. רבי מאיר's strictness may not carry over to חופה.

steps.title: Maybe רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון are lenient only about קידושין
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון might be lenient only about קידושין, because חופה is close to actual living together and could disqualify her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else: perhaps רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון only said this there about קידושין, which is not close to ביאה. But חופה, which is close to ביאה, may well disqualify her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks out the other side of the comparison. Even the lenient תנאים might be strict about חופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין is far from the couple actually living together, so it makes sense that it would not disqualify her. חופה is the stage right before ביאה, so it might count more. So we cannot say for sure that the lenient view about קידושין is also lenient about חופה.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively, or else
Close to marital relations
So too, indeed

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides of the first proposed link fail. קידושין and חופה differ in two ways: קידושין acquires her, while חופה is closer to ביאה. So each תנא might rule differently about חופה than about קידושין.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי
phrases.english: Alternatively: they only said it
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon, there,
about betrothal, which is not close to intercourse,
but the wedding canopy, which is close to intercourse,
indeed, it may disqualify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel rejection, this time aimed at the lenient side of the argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The part of the proof that relies on רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חופה is closer to ביאה than קידושין is, so their leniency may not carry over to חופה.

steps.title: A new attempt: a ברייתא about women who entered the חופה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different argument among תנאים, found in a ברייתא that speaks directly about women who entered the חופה but did not yet live with their husbands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a source, it is the argument of these תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: If they married, whether the women were fit or unfit, or they entered the חופה but did not yet have relations, they eat from his food and they eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first comparison and brings a new source, a ברייתא that talks about חופה directly. Its first opinion is quoted here. The opposing opinion comes in step 7, after the גמרא clarifies this wording in steps 5 and 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is a better source because it does not need to compare קידושין with חופה; it addresses חופה itself. Its first opinion says that even unfit women who entered the חופה may still eat תרומה. In other words, by this view חופה does not disqualify her.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, if there is anything to say (if any source exists)
In the argument of these other תנאים
It was taught in a ברייתא
Women fit and unfit (to marry a כהן)
They eat תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: Only the first opinion of the ברייתא appears here. Do not take its lenient ruling as the final word; the opposing opinion of the other תנא appears in step 7.

phrases.english: Rather, if there is anything to say,
it is in the argument of these תנאים, as it was taught:
If they married, both kinds, fit and unfit,
phrases.notes: "Unfit" means a woman this כהן is not allowed to marry.

phrases.english: or they entered the wedding canopy and did not have relations,
they eat from his food, and they eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר, בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proposed link was rejected, the גמרא offers a new source that deals with חופה directly.
steps.raayaObject: That whether חופה disqualifies her from תרומה is an argument among תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about fit and unfit women who entered the חופה without ביאה; its first opinion says they still eat תרומה

steps.title: Does 'they married' mean real married life?
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא later says 'they entered' the חופה, the earlier word 'they married' seems to mean real married life with living together. But that cannot be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They entered.' This implies that 'they married' means really married, including living together?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to question the wording of the ברייתא it just quoted. If 'they married' means real married life, the ברייתא would not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seems to describe two cases: 'they married' and 'they entered the חופה.' If these were two separate cases, 'they married' would have to mean actual living together. But a forbidden woman who lived with the כהן is disqualified from תרומה, so she could not be eating תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: they entered (into the חופה)
this implies that
they married
really, actually

phrases.english: 'They entered' implies that 'they married'
phrases.notes: Both words come from the ברייתא quoted in step 4.

phrases.english: means really married?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the wording of the ברייתא brought in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's two expressions, 'they married' and 'they entered.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If these are two separate cases, 'they married' must mean living together. But then the forbidden woman could not eat תרומה.

steps.title: It is one case: entered the חופה without living together
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is really describing a single case: the couple entered the חופה but did not live together. The ברייתא says such women may eat his food and eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it talking about a case where they entered the חופה but did not live together? And it teaches: they eat from his food and they eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. 'They married' and 'they entered' describe one case: חופה without living together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we read the ברייתא this way, the first opinion in it clearly holds that חופה alone lets the woman eat תרומה. Only actual living together would disqualify her. This sets up one side of the argument the גמרא is looking for.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, isn't it that
and they did not live together (as husband and wife)
and it teaches
they eat תרומה

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it a case where they entered the wedding canopy
and did not live together?
And it teaches: they eat from his food
and they eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ לְחוּפָּה וְלֹא נִבְעֲלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: two expressions describe one case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'They married' and 'they entered' are two separate cases, so 'they married' means living together.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both describe one case, חופה without living together, and the ברייתא lets such women eat תרומה.

steps.title: The opposing view: חופה works only where living together would
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says that if living together would not let her eat תרומה, then חופה does not let her either. This seems to be a direct argument about חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: any woman whose living together lets her eat תרומה, her חופה lets her eat. Any woman whose living together does not let her eat, her חופה does not let her eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion that disagrees with the first. This completes the proof: here are תנאים who argue about חופה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said a forbidden woman may eat תרומה after חופה. רבי ישמעאל ties חופה to living together. Since living together would disqualify a forbidden woman, her חופה cannot let her eat. So it looks like the open question about חופה is really this argument between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: her living together (with the husband)
lets her eat (תרומה)
her wedding canopy, her entering the חופה

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion in the ברייתא: חופה lets a forbidden woman eat תרומה. רבי ישמעאל: חופה works only where living together would also work.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:
Any woman whose living together lets her eat תרומה,
her wedding canopy lets her eat;
and any woman whose living together does not let her eat,
her wedding canopy does not let her eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 4 by giving the opposing view in the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the question about חופה is an argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: the first opinion lets her eat after חופה, and רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה does not.

steps.title: Maybe רבי ישמעאל just follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Perhaps רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי מאיר, who forbids תרומה even after קידושין, so this is not a separate argument about חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, holds like רבי מאיר, who said that with קידושין she does not eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the ברייתא. It suggests a different way to understand רבי ישמעאל's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר already holds that a forbidden woman may not eat תרומה after קידושין (step 1). If רבי ישמעאל simply agrees with רבי מאיר, his ruling about חופה is just part of that known strictness. Then this ברייתא only repeats the argument about קידושין and does not prove a separate argument about חופה.

keyTerms.meaning: from where (do you know)?
perhaps
he holds (this opinion)
betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.whatToRemember: The proof is rejected. רבי ישמעאל's strict view may come from agreeing with רבי מאיר about קידושין, not from a special rule about חופה.

phrases.english: From where do you know this?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka,
holds like Rabbi Meir,
who said that with betrothal she does not eat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ברייתא as an independent argument about חופה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי ישמעאל's ruling may simply follow רבי מאיר's strict view about קידושין. It need not be a separate opinion about חופה.

steps.title: Why would he mention חופה and not קידושין?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי מאיר, his statement should have spoken about קידושין money, not חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this line, 'Any woman whose living together does not let her eat, her חופה does not let her eat', is hard. He should have said, 'Any woman whose living together does not let her eat, her קידושין money does not let her eat'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection in step 8. If רבי ישמעאל holds like רבי מאיר, his words do not fit that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, the woman already loses תרומה at the moment of קידושין. So if רבי ישמעאל agreed with him, he should have said that her קידושין does not let her eat. His choice of the word חופה suggests he really is talking about חופה.

keyTerms.meaning: Her money: the money used for קידושין
He should have said
Lets her eat (תרומה)

phrases.english: This line: 'Any woman whose living together does not let her eat'
'her חופה does not let her eat'
'Any woman whose living together does not let her eat'
'her money does not let her eat' is what he should have said!
phrases.notes: 'Her money' means the קידושין money, since for רבי מאיר the problem already starts at קידושין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection given in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי מאיר's view the woman is cut off from תרומה at קידושין, so naming חופה does not fit.

steps.title: He just followed the first תנא's wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל said חופה only because the תנא קמא had spoken about חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps, since the תנא קמא said 'חופה', he too said 'חופה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rejection. רבי ישמעאל used the word חופה only to match the earlier speaker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חופה does not prove what רבי ישמעאל really holds. He was answering in the same terms as the תנא קמא. So the ברייתא still cannot prove a separate argument about חופה.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because of (here: since the other one already said it)
The first, unnamed תנא in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא, אַיְּידֵי דְּאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא חוּפָּה
phrases.english: Perhaps, since the first תנא said 'חופה'
he too said 'חופה'.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל cannot prove an argument about חופה. He may agree with רבי מאיר and simply be using the תנא קמא's word.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording as following the other speaker's language
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word חופה shows רבי ישמעאל was making his own point about חופה
steps.terutzMaskana: He only borrowed the תנא קמא's word, so nothing is proven

steps.title: רב ששת: a חופה with an unfit woman still counts
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם reports that רב ששת taught, with support from a משנה, that a חופה with a woman unfit for her husband is still a real חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: רב ששת told us this matter, and he lit up our eyes from a משנה: there is חופה for unfit women.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רב עמרם reports רב ששת's rule that a חופה counts even with a woman who is forbidden to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that a חופה with a forbidden woman means nothing legally. רב ששת says it still has the force of a real חופה. רב עמרם adds that רב ששת showed this from a משנה, which the גמרא is about to bring.

keyTerms.meaning: Women who are unfit to marry this man, for example women forbidden to a כהן
And he lit up our eyes: he showed us clearly

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the center of the rest of the sugya. The next steps test the משנה that is meant to support it.

phrases.english: רב עמרם said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִילְּתָא אֲמַר לַן רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
phrases.english: This matter רב ששת told us
and he lit up our eyes from a משנה:
There is חופה for unfit women.
phrases.notes: He means a חופה still counts as a real חופה even when the woman is forbidden to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם: הָא מִילְּתָא אֲמַר לַן רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the significance of חופה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חופה with a woman unfit for her husband still has legal force.

steps.title: Support from the סוטה oath
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about סוטה says she answers אמן that she did not stray as an ארוסה, a נשואה, a שומרת יבם, or a כנוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא also taught it: 'Amen, that I did not stray as a betrothed woman or a married woman, as one waiting for her יבם, or as one taken in by him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that רב ששת used. The סוטה's oath includes the time when she was only an ארוסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath covers straying while she was only betrothed. That only makes sense in some special case. The גמרא will now work out what that case is and how it supports רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא taught it too: a source that agrees
I strayed (was unfaithful)
A widow waiting for her יבם
Taken in: married to the יבם

phrases.english: And the תנא also taught it:
'Amen, that I did not stray'
phrases.notes: This is the סוטה answering the כהן's oath before she drinks the bitter waters.

phrases.english: 'as a betrothed woman or a married woman,'
'as one waiting for her יבם, or as one taken in by him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה that supports רב ששת
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's rule that a חופה with an unfit woman counts
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the סוטה oath

steps.title: What case is the 'ארוסה' in the oath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation the משנה means when it mentions an ארוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ארוסה: what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact case behind the word ארוסה. This sets up the attempts that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the משנה can prove anything, the גמרא needs a case where an ארוסה could be part of a סוטה oath. Each suggestion that follows will be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
A woman who has had קידושין but not yet נישואין

phrases.english: This betrothed woman, what is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case behind the משנה just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact situation of the ארוסה in the oath

steps.title: A betrothed woman never drinks
steps.stepSummary: If he warned her and makes her drink while she is still an ארוסה, that is impossible, because a משנה says an ארוסה does not drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he warned her while she was betrothed and makes her drink while she is betrothed, is a betrothed woman fit to drink? But we learned: a betrothed woman and a שומרת יבם do not drink and do not collect a כתובה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simplest case and rejects it at once using another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waters of סוטה apply only to a married woman. So the oath cannot be about a woman who is still only betrothed when she drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: He warned her (קינוי) not to be alone with a certain man
Fit to drink the waters of סוטה
The marriage contract money

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the time of the warning with the time of drinking. This first attempt has both happen while she is an ארוסה; the next attempt separates them.

phrases.english: If you say he warned her when she was betrothed
and makes her drink when she is betrothed
is a betrothed woman fit to drink?
But didn't we learn:
A betrothed woman and one waiting for her יבם
do not drink and do not collect a כתובה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a first case for step 13 and knocks it down
steps.kashyaTarget: The case where the warning and the drinking both happen while she is an ארוסה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that an ארוסה does not drink at all

steps.title: Warned while betrothed, drinks after the wedding
steps.stepSummary: Second attempt: he warned her while she was betrothed, she secluded herself, and he makes her drink after they are married.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he warned her while she was betrothed and she secluded herself, and he makes her drink when she is married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new case: the warning and seclusion happened while she was an ארוסה, and the drinking happens after נישואין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now she is married when she drinks, so the problem from step 14 is gone. The oath still covers what she did as an ארוסה.

keyTerms.meaning: She secluded herself with the man she was warned about
A fully married woman

phrases.english: Rather, he warned her when she was betrothed
and she secluded herself,
and he makes her drink when she is married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the case rejected in step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warning and seclusion were while she was betrothed, and the drinking is after נישואין.

steps.title: The waters would not test her
steps.stepSummary: In that case the husband is not 'clean of sin', and the ברייתא says the waters then do not test his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do the waters test her? But it was taught: 'And the man shall be clear of sin.' When the man is clear of sin, the waters test his wife. When the man is not clear of sin, the waters do not test his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second case. Since the husband married her after she secluded herself, the waters will not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she secluded herself after a warning, she became forbidden to him. By marrying her anyway, he is not 'clear of sin'. The ברייתא says the waters work only when the husband is clear of sin, so this case fails too.

keyTerms.meaning: The waters test her
'And the man shall be clear of sin' (במדבר 5:31)
Clean of sin

phrases.english: Do the waters test her?
But wasn't it taught:
'And the man shall be clear of sin':
When the man is clear of sin
the waters test his wife;
if the man is not clear of sin
phrases.notes: Here he married her after she secluded herself, when she was already forbidden to him.

phrases.english: the waters do not test his wife.

steps.whatToRemember: Both cases tried so far fail. An ארוסה cannot drink, and if she secluded herself before the wedding, the husband is not 'clear of sin', so the waters will not test her.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case suggested in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of a warning and seclusion while betrothed, with drinking after the wedding
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband married a woman who was forbidden to him, so he is not clear of sin, and the waters do not test his wife.

steps.title: Third attempt: warned while betrothed, then entered the חופה with no relations
steps.stepSummary: The ארוסה case means he warned her while she was betrothed, she secluded herself, and then she entered the חופה but he never had relations with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he warned her while she was betrothed, she secluded herself, and then she entered the wedding canopy but he did not have relations with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that avoids both earlier problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She now drinks as a married woman, so the rule that an ארוסה does not drink is not a problem (Step 14). Since the husband never had relations with her after the seclusion, he is still 'clean of sin', so the problem from Step 16 is gone too.

keyTerms.meaning: he warned her (gave her a jealousy warning)
she secluded herself with the other man
the wedding canopy, the step that makes her fully married
she had relations

phrases.english: Rather, he warned her when she was betrothed,
and she secluded herself,
and she entered the wedding canopy but did not have relations

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of Step 15, which was rejected in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ארוסה case does the משנה mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Warned and secluded as an ארוסה, then a חופה without relations, so she drinks as a married woman and the husband is clean of sin.

steps.title: Learn from this: a חופה counts even with forbidden women
steps.stepSummary: Since the waters test her after this חופה, a חופה has legal force even when the woman is forbidden to the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: a wedding canopy counts even for women who are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a rule from the case it just set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the seclusion she was forbidden to her husband, yet the חופה still made her a 'married woman' who drinks. So a חופה works even with a פסולה, which is the point the larger sugya is trying to prove.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from this
a חופה counts even with women who are forbidden to the man

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the conclusion the whole line of questions was working toward, so the next steps test whether it really holds.

phrases.english: And learn from this
there is a wedding canopy for unfit women.
phrases.notes: He means a חופה still has legal effect even when the woman is forbidden to the man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a rule from the case defined in Step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A חופה has legal force even with a woman forbidden to the man.

steps.title: רבא: the waters only work if the husband was with her first
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא: 'besides your husband' means the waters test her only if the husband had relations with her before the other man did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Do you think this is a solid answer? When רבי אחא בר חנינא came from the South, he brought a ברייתא: 'besides your husband' means a woman whose husband was with her before the other man, not one where the other man was with her before the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the answer in Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17 the husband never had relations with her, so the other man was first. According to this ברייתא, the waters would not test her at all, so the case cannot be the one the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: and do you really think so?
a solid, well-fitting answer
'besides your husband' (from the סוטה oath)
the other man who had relations with her

phrases.english: Rava said:
And do you think that this is a solid answer?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא מִדָּרוֹמָא,
phrases.english: But when Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina came from the South,
he came and brought a baraita in his hand:
"Besides your husband",
one whose husband's lying with her came before the other man's,
and not one where the other man's lying came before the husband's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְתִסְבְּרָא דְּהָא מְתָרַצְתָּא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case in Step 17 and with it the proof in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of a חופה without relations (Step 17).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The waters only test her if the husband was with her before the other man; in Step 17 the husband never was, so she could not drink.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: the betrothed husband was with her in her father's house
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the betrothed husband had relations with her in her father's house before the warning, so he came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: You can find it where her betrothed had relations with her in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא saves the answer of Step 17 by adding a detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband had relations with her earlier, while she was still an ארוסה in her father's house, so his relations came before the other man's and רבא's ברייתא is satisfied. She was still only an ארוסה, then she was warned, secluded, and entered the חופה, so the proof that יש חופה לפסולות stands.

keyTerms.meaning: you can find the case
her father's house, before she moved in with the husband

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
You can find it

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּא עָלֶיהָ אֲרוּסָהּ בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ.
phrases.english: such as where her betrothed had relations with her in her father's house.
phrases.notes: This was before the warning, so the husband came first. He stays clean of sin because he never lived with her after she secluded herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case by adding a detail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband never had relations with her, so the waters cannot work.
steps.terutzMaskana: He had relations with her earlier in her father's house, so he came first and the waters do work.

steps.title: Setting up the parallel case of a שומרת יבם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask about the matching case of a שומרת יבם, where the יבם had relations with her in her father-in-law's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same kind of case for a שומרת יבם would be where the יבם had relations with her in her father-in-law's house,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by building a matching case for a שומרת יבם. The question itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה also mentions a שומרת יבם, so the גמרא tries to apply רמי בר חמא's idea to her. The parallel would be relations with the יבם in her father-in-law's house, and the problem with that case comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: the matching case
a widow waiting for her husband's brother to do יבום
her father-in-law's house

phrases.english: The matching case regarding a widow waiting for her yavam —
where the yavam had relations with her in her father-in-law's house,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רמי בר חמא's answer from Step 20 to the שומרת יבם in the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's case, tested on the שומרת יבם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Builds the parallel case; the actual difficulty is stated on the next amud.
